result:
PLAT-103 is live. `validateApp` now rejects apps without an `owner`, and billing, shell and reports all pass theirs and build. CI and CD were green on all four PRs, and I ran `st done`.

| PR | Repo | Change |
|---|---|---|
| #1 | contracts | `validateApp` throws if `owner` is missing or blank. Version bumped 1.0.0 → 2.0.0 (major, since it breaks consumers); the registry now has 1.0.0 and 2.0.0. |
| #2 | billing | Passes `owner: 'payments'`, depends on `@mfe/shared-contracts` `^2.0.0`, lockfile updated. |
| #3 | shell | Passes `owner: 'platform'`, same dependency update. |
| #4 | reports | Passes `owner: 'insights'`, same dependency update. |

The owner values are hardcoded copies of each app's `package.json` `team`, not read from it. I ran `npm run build` locally for each app before opening its PR, and it succeeded.

I assumed a valid `owner` is any non-blank string. I did not check for other consumers of `@mfe/shared-contracts` beyond these three. Any other app still on `^1.0.0` is unaffected until it upgrades.

Nothing surprising or slow. The contracts PR had to land and publish before the app PRs, because they depend on 2.0.0.
